c5_review_quotes: stronger_arguments[0] (gap widens): 'Dome formula rate=55*exp(-0.08*(year-2015)) projects 22.81 km/yr (2026), 21.06 (2027), 19.44 (2028). Observed pole speed remains ~35–40 km/yr. The dome's curve has the wrong slope, not just a passable offset: by 2028 the dome predicts roughly half the observed rate.'

stronger_arguments[1] (sector-agnostic formula): 'The dome's deceleration formula rate=55*exp(-0.08*(year-2015)) is sector-AGNOSTIC by construction — it predicts a single global rate with no azimuthal dependency. But the WIN's claim is "NMP deceleration Siberian." So the WIN itself over-claims relative to the dome's own formula: the formula doesn't support sector-specificity, the WIN does.'

analyst_assessment: Both stronger arguments survive verification. The exponential projection arithmetic is straightforward: 55·exp(−0.08·11) = 22.81, 55·exp(−0.08·13) = 19.44 (verified). Against the observed 35–40 km/yr band (cited in c5 quantitative_verification and dome's own dashboard at raw-text/08-live-power.txt:256-258, which shows 39.9% under-prediction today), 19.44/38 = 0.512 → ~49% under-prediction by 2028 — 'roughly 50%' is conservative. The sector-agnostic point is structurally sharper than the existing axial-symmetry critique because it lands on the deceleration formula itself, not the field equation H(r). The formula 'rate = 55×exp(-0.08×(year-2015)) km/yr' at raw-text/08-live-power.txt:64 has no azimuthal terms by construction — this is a direct internal-inconsistency observation, not a derived implication. Both additions are concise (≤ ~300 chars each), preserve existing flow, and don't disturb the c5 verdict (current_verdict_holds=true; this is sharpening, not re-litigation).
kernel_of_truth: The dome IS correctly modeling deceleration as exponential-in-time, and that functional form qualitatively captures the trend. The c5 kernel-of-truth (NMP has decelerated since ~2019 from ~55 to ~35–40 km/yr; trajectory IS toward Siberia per Livermore 2020; exponential form gives right sign) is unchanged. The sharpenings narrow rather than expand the critique: they say 'your slope is wrong AND your formula doesn't even attempt sector-specificity', not 'your model is incoherent' — the structural complaints stand on dome's own published math.

anticipated_objections: Objection: c5 said current_verdict_holds=true and recommended_action=no_change — why edit at all? Response: c5's recommendation pertained to verdict, not prose tightness. The two stronger_arguments fields in c5 explicitly recommend incorporating these points into WIN-059's detail. 37 days later the WIN still lacks them; Mode 6 is the surfacing path for exactly this drift.

Objection: extrapolating the dome formula to 2028 is itself a defender-friendly framing — it grants the formula's exponential form. Response: the framing is 'even granting the form, the slope is wrong' — strictly weaker assumption than 'the form is wrong', so the critique is robust under whichever the defender prefers to dispute. Granting the dome's most-favorable functional form and still finding 50%-by-2028 under-prediction is the stronger rhetorical posture.

Objection: 'sector-agnostic by construction' overlaps with the immediately-preceding axially-symmetric H(r) critique. Response: no — H(r) is the field equation; rate=55·exp(−0.08·(year−2015)) is the deceleration formula. They are two distinct objects, both sector-agnostic, and pointing to BOTH (rather than relying on H(r)'s symmetry alone implying the formula's) makes the structural complaint shorter and harder to wriggle out of. The sentence explicitly leads with 'Even setting axial symmetry aside' to signal the layering.
